subject: Quantum Health: on-prem adoption assessment — technical & operational details
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@quantumhealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Josh Lim <josh.lim@quantumhealth.com>; procurement@quantumhealth.com
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Quantum Health: on-prem adoption assessment — detailed capability ask

Irene —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we evaluate moving a subset of inference traffic to an on‑prem footprint, procurement and our infra team asked for a deeper capability anchor than the PPT. Can you share detailed answers to the following so we can complete our internal RFP matrix?

1) Installation modes supported (air‑gapped, internet‑limited, VPC with egress proxies) and the operator actions required for each.
2) Minimum and recommended hardware profiles (GPUs, disk IO, network) for 2 production pods serving 8 concurrent sessions at 2k token average.
3) Lifecycle ops: patching model updates, OS/agent updates, and rollback procedures — how do you support patch automation in air‑gapped sites?
4) Controls: KMS/HSM integration, local audit logs format (can we ingest into our Splunk?), identity/SSO options (SCIM/SAML), and emergency access procedures.
5) Evidence: a sample runbook, install checklist, and a simple network diagram we can drop into our change board.

I've attached our internal list (quantum_deployment_requirements_080121.pdf). We're on a tight timeline — procurement hopes to close a feasibility decision by EOD next Friday.

If it's helpful we can do a 30‑minute call to walk through.

Best,
Sanjay Rao
Director, IT Infrastructure
Quantum Health

Attachments: quantum_deployment_requirements_080121.pdf (pdf, 210KB)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 17:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quantum Health: on-prem adoption assessment — detailed capability ask

Sanjay —

Thanks for the clear list. Below are concise answers; I attached a more formal PDF summary and a one‑page operator checklist for your change board. If you want we can schedule a 30‑minute technical handoff with Marcus and our field ops team tomorrow.

1) Installation modes
- Air‑gapped: Supported via our offline installer bundle. Operators copy the signed installer tarball + model artifacts via USB or secure file transfer. Installer validates checksums and performs local KMS bootstrapping with customer HSM (we support PKCS#11 and AWS CloudHSM agent proxy). No outbound connections required.
- Internet‑limited (egress proxy): Supported. The node agent can be configured to use an HTTP(S) proxy and allowlist our verification endpoints. Artifact verification occurs via signed manifests cached locally.
- VPC (private cloud): Standard supported deployment — private control plane option available where customer retains VPC peering and private links.

Operator actions: provide host inventory, open ports in the change ticket we list on p.4 of the attached; provide HSM credentials to the local operator agent, and optionally appoint an operator service account for SCIM.

2) Hardware profiles (for 2 pods serving ~8 concurrent sessions @ ~2k tokens avg)
- Minimum (dev/test): 2 x A10G (or equivalent T4 alternatives), 256GB RAM, 2TB NVMe (high write).
- Recommended (production): 2 x A100 40GB or L40S class GPUs per pod, 512GB RAM, NVMe RAID1, 40Gbps NIC. Expect ~120–180ms p95 per 2k token request under continuous batching; batching policies will change that.
- Disk IO: 2.0 GB/s sustained preferred for swap and model loading spikes.

3) Lifecycle ops
- Model rollout: model artifacts are versioned and signed. We support canary rollout with traffic split at the router; operator may pin specific model hashes per route.
- Patching: For air‑gapped sites we provide a signed patch bundle. Operators upload it to the bootstrap host; the agent runs a preflight and staged apply with rollback markers. For VPC sites, we support staged patch orchestration through our Private control plane via a secure TLS tunnel.
- Rollback: Automatic rollback on health checks + manual rollback via CLI with model hash or snapshot id.

4) Controls
- KMS/HSM: Integrations: PKCS#11, AWS CloudHSM via proxy, Azure Dedicated HSM (customers manage keys); we offer envelope encryption and local key wrapping.
- Logs/audit: Local audit logs are JSONL with RFC3339 timestamps — we provide a Splunk ingestion config (attached). Logs include operator actions, model load events, and token-level cost summaries (configurable sampling).
- Identity: SAML 2.0 for SSO + SCIM for provisioning. Fine‑grained RBAC for operators + emergency breakglass keys with time‑boxed access in the operator CLI.

5) Evidence: attached: redwood_private_capabilities_summary_v2.pdf (detailed answers), operator_oncall_checklist.xlsx (operator runbook), network_diagram_template.yaml (simple VPC topology).

Next steps
- I'll loop Marcus for a short ops kick‑off to validate network ports and GPU targets.
- Vanessa will follow up on commercial and procurement considerations.

If that works, propose Wed 08/22 10:00am PT for a 30‑minute call.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Head of Field Solutions
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415‑555‑0218

Attachments: redwood_private_capabilities_summary_v2.pdf (pdf, 420KB); operator_oncall_checklist.xlsx (xlsx, 48KB); network_diagram_template.yaml (yaml, 3KB)

Irene/Marcus —

Looping in commercial notes for Sanjay's timeline. Quick bullets for response:
- We can provide a 12‑month reserved configuration discount if they commit to 2 pods (savings table in the redwood_private_capabilities_summary_v2.pdf).
- For air‑gapped installs, add a professional services line for onsite operator training (2 days) and install validation. Estimate: $12,000 flat.
- SLA / credits: we can accept a standard enterprise SLA for Dedicated; for Private (air‑gapped) SLA is operationally limited — propose 99.5% with defined operator response times.
- Procurement ask: we should push MOA + mutual data handling addendum — I can share a DocuSign envelope once we confirm scope.

Irene — can you confirm whether the installed agent requires outbound callbacks for license verification after first boot? That will be a gating item for their security team.

V.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 23 Aug 2028 10:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quantum Health: on-prem adoption assessment — technical clarifications

Irene/Vanessa —

Quick technical clarifications to add to the PDF before we send to their infra team:

- License verification: The agent performs a one‑time outbound signature check at first activation (TLS to our signing endpoint). After the initial activation, license verification can be switched to offline via a signed token file that your security officer can host locally. No periodic callbacks are required unless you enable feature telemetry.
- Model loading: For large models we stream shards from local NVMe instead of memory‑mapping to reduce swap spikes. We recommend preloading models during a maintenance window; attach a preload cmd in the operator checklist.
- Network ports: Minimum open list — TCP 443 outbound (activation), 22 (ops SSH if approved), 50051 (gRPC internal), 15000–15010 (router health + admin). See network_diagram_template.yaml for examples.
- Hardware note: If they plan for quantized LLMs (8‑bit), L40S or A100 40GB are preferred for latency parity; M60/T4 class GPUs will see p95 regressions.

I attached a small example network diagram template and a short step for preload + health probe I want in the final runbook. I'll also include a suggested cc list of their infra folks (they didn't include names for the infra owners in the initial ask).

-Marcus
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: network_diagram_template.yaml (yaml, 3KB)
